messages.author: 065df7db94921700
messages.subject: Shiny ReactiveUI
parts:
The addition of this function is fantastic.  It allows for a much greater flexibility in my webapps; however, if I could make a suggestion to the Shiny developers:

Adding a new function to pass commands directly to the browser console will make the interface drastically more flexible, and allow for full implementation of d3 commands within R.  All that is necessary is a command, such as:

ConsoleCommand('var header = d3.select("#chart").append("svg:svg")
.attr("width", window.innerWidth)
.attr("height", 50)
.append("text")
.attr("id", "header")
.attr("dy", 25)
.attr("dx", "50%")
.text(headerText);')

This would only require the addition of the following to the Shiny JavaScript:

function onMessage(msg) {
eval(msg.data);
}

I can do some of these commands by including the string as a command in the ReactiveUI function; however, this method would be faster and would not require modifying the HTML file for every command.  Unfortunately, I am not able to implement this change myself by adding a js file to the app folder because I have no way to access the value of the websocket in order to use websocket_write(command, WS).  As an aside, accessing this value would be beneficial for apps that require significant calculation time in R, e.g. Markov chain Monte Carlo methods where I would prefer to update the app during a function that may take a few hours to complete.  Like I said, the ReactiveUI function is a great addition and has a lot of potential for fully integrating R into the web.

-Chris

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Shiny ReactiveUI
parts:
Hi Chris,

I'm a little leery of making this a supported idiom, as it cuts against the grain of the Shiny model to want something done "right now"--it's more imperative while the Shiny model is more declarative.

That said, I would love to let you do some hacking on this albeit in a not-officially-supported way. I believe you can write directly to the websocket from within server.R like this:

.subset2(input, "impl")$.websocket$send(foo)

where foo is either a raw vector or UTF-8 encoded string.

You'll want to use the GitHub version of Shiny [devtools::install_github("shiny", "rstudio")] as it moves away from the "websockets" package and depends on our new "httpuv" package instead.

It looks to me like you've discovered the oncustommessage hook in shiny.js, which you can override by setting Shiny.oncustommessage; that's really the only other piece you need. I will find it slightly surprising though if you don't run into challenges trying to get these messages sent to the client at exactly the right time.

Good luck!

messages.author: 55771919c42cb6a1
messages.subject: Re: Shiny ReactiveUI
parts:
While working a different issue, I actually implemented something that allows sending arbitrary Javascript from the server to the client -- but I ended up not keeping this code for that issue. However, I've cleaned it up and put it in this branch:
  https://github.com/wch/shiny/tree/eval-js

You can install with:
  devtools::install_github('shiny', 'wch', 'eval-js')
You will also need to have httpuv.


I've modified the 01_hello example to demonstrate how to use it:
  https://gist.github.com/wch/5202490

On the server end, you add an evalJsHandler like this:
  output$test_eval <- evalJsHandler({
    paste("alert('Hello World! obs is ", input$obs, ".');", sep = "")
  })

Somewhere in ui.r, you add a jsEvaluator:
    jsEvaluator("test_eval")


I don't know if this will actually be useful for your particular case, since the server doesn't necessarily send the Javascript immediately to the client. It will send the Javascript code along with everything else, when all the reactive outputs have finished executing and their output is flushed (I think).

Please keep in mind that this is at best something to experiment with. If we were to add something like this for real, we'd need to consider more carefully the design and implementation.

-Winston

messages.author: 065df7db94921700
messages.subject: Re: Shiny ReactiveUI
parts:
Thank you both for your suggestions.  The shiny package has proven useful for most applications, but the time-intensive functions have given me issues since I do not want the user to wait for hours without receiving any updates on the MCMC method progress.  I have manually built an interface with the Websockets package, but I too have run into issues with the file upload.  I will see what I can figure out with these suggestions.

-Chris

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Shiny ReactiveUI
parts:
Thanks for the feedback. The issue of progress is important and one we hope to address in a future release of Shiny.

In the meantime if you do end up needing to build your own thing, I recommend doing it on top of httpuv if possible. The limitations of the websockets package are pretty structural which is why we had to rewrite from scratch instead of just fixing websockets to properly support file uploads.
